persona: OR engineer who wants to tune PyVRP; starts from examples/pyvrp/README.md and follows section 6 literally, using <repo>\.venv-pyvrp\Scripts\python.exe (PyVRP 0.14.0). Providers used: fake and param_lhs only. All work in $S (called $S below).
journey: 16:55 read examples/pyvrp/README.md, root README, docs/new-experiment.md, AGENTS.md, evolvekit.yaml / evolvekit.real.yaml and the CLI --help pages. 16:56 started the section-6 offline run in the background with --run-dir $S/runs/pyvrp and stdout redirected to a log, then watched from a second shell with `status`, `leaderboard`, and by listing the run dir. The redirected log stayed empty for the whole run (all output arrived at exit); `status` said "no runs recorded" for the first 20 s, then showed only the seed until generation 1 ended, although a child's stage_out JSON had been on disk for 16+ s. The run finished in 1m50s (README: about two minutes), exit 0, improvement 0. Ran `preflight` on the offline config (clean, 23 s) - the same seed/same --seed scored EUR 2,180 there vs EUR 2,076 in the run a minute earlier. Reproduced the 300-order/20 s baseline with evaluate.py (EUR 2,076, matches README 2,075.5). Generated one 3000-order instance into scratch (0.34 s) and confirmed it loads with skeleton.load_instance/build_data (3,105 locations, 261 vehicles); there is no documented command for that, I wrote a 6-line snippet. Then tried my own problem: copied the example to $S/own, added a 3-instance set to INPUT_SETS, wrote own.yaml (extends, seeds: 2, --time-limit 3, param_lhs). preflight failed with only "exit code 1": the copied evaluate.py could no longer find .venv-pyvrp and bare `python` is the system interpreter (PyVRP 0.13.4). `run` aborted correctly on the failed seed but exited 0. After hard-coding the venv interpreter in the stage command, preflight and a 1m40s run succeeded (17:04:40). That run reported a 1.3 % "improvement" while the 2-seed objective CV was 2.4-2.6 %, and still made 2 fake LLM calls because `extends` merged my operators map with the base. A hold-out variant showed the hold-out also runs seeds: 2, which contradicts the wall-clock figures documented for evolvekit.real.yaml. No 120 s / 900 s solves were run. Resume was not tried. Never read evolvekit/*.py or tests/. Both run PIDs I started (7568, 10028) have exited; repo left untouched (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 used so evaluate.py would not drop a __pycache__ into examples/pyvrp).

entries.title: Wall-clock-bounded scoring: identical seed config swings 5 % between two evaluations a minute apart, and a within-noise gain is reported as an improvement
entries.step: Comparing the seed's score in the offline run with the seed's score in preflight, then judging whether my own run's 'improvement' was real
entries.command: .venv-pyvrp/Scripts/python.exe -m evolvekit run --config examples/pyvrp/evolvekit.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/pyvrp   (16:56)  then  .venv-pyvrp/Scripts/python.exe -m evolvekit preflight --config examples/pyvrp/evolvekit.yaml   (16:58); later  python -m evolvekit run --config own.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/own
entries.observed: run, seed g000-c0001: 'metro-300-s7: feasible, objective EUR 2,076 after 2,808 iterations in 20.2s of a 20s budget.'  preflight, same skeleton, same --seed 42, one minute later: 'metro-300-s7: feasible, objective EUR 2,180 after 1,228 iterations in 20.6s of a 20s budget.'  (standalone evaluate.py: 3,487 iterations, EUR 2,076). Children in the demo differ from the seed by 0.1-0.4 % (-2100.53 / -2102.37 / -2103.18). Own run summary: 'seed score : -900.102  best score : -888.313  improvement : 11.7896' while runs.jsonl kpi_cv.objective for those rows is 0.0264 (seed) and 0.0238 (winner), i.e. a 1.3 % gain against a 2.4-2.6 % CV. Nothing in run output, status, leaderboard or the HTML flags this.
entries.expected: Either a scoring mode that is not decided by background load (iteration-bounded proxy, or paired re-evaluation of the incumbent alongside challengers), or at least every view showing iterations and kpi_cv and marking improvements smaller than the measured noise as 'within noise'. README section 3 says noise is 'a few tenths of a percent'; I measured 5 % on a busy machine.
entries.why_it_matters: I would ship a PyVRP parameter set chosen by whichever candidate happened to be evaluated while the machine was quiet. On the real config each such mistake costs an hour of solver time and the run's 'best' is not trustworthy.
entries.suggested_fix: Print iterations and objective CV next to every score; label d-best smaller than max(epsilon, k x CV) as 'within noise'; document (or add) an iteration-bounded stop for proxy stages; optionally re-evaluate the current best in the same generation so comparisons are made under the same load; have preflight run the seed twice and report the spread even when seeds: 1.

entries.title: Documented wall clock for evolvekit.real.yaml is off by about 2x: the hold-out also runs seeds: N
entries.step: Working out what one full-stage evaluation of the real config costs before committing a machine to it
entries.command: cd $S/own && python -m evolvekit preflight --config own-holdout.yaml   (own config: stage full with seeds: 2, inputs: [test3], private_inputs: [test3], --time-limit 3)
entries.observed: 'stage full                 ok      19.4s x2 seed(s)  (timeout 60s per run)' and 'stage full (hold-out)      ok      19.3s x2 seed(s)  (timeout 60s per run)'. So private_inputs are solved once per seed too. evolvekit.real.yaml has 'seeds: 2' on the full stage, yet its comments say 'Stage 2 is 900 s on the public instance plus 900 s on the private hold-out, so 30 minutes per candidate' and 'Six full evaluations a day. Each is 900 s public + 900 s private, so this is three hours of solver'; README section 4 says 'then 2 x 30 minutes of full stage - roughly 70-80 minutes' per generation; README section 8 says '9 full evaluations of 3 x 900 s each'; root README says '900 s x 2 seeds full -> 900 s private hold-out'.
entries.expected: One consistent figure. By my scaled-down measurement a full evaluation is 4 x ~913 s = ~61 min, a generation with top_k_per_generation: 2 is ~2 h 10 min (not 70-80), and max_full_evals_per_day: 6 is ~6 h of solver (not 3).
entries.why_it_matters: I plan machine time and the daily cap from these numbers. A 20-generation run is ~43 h instead of the ~25 h the docs imply; I could not verify with the real config because a 900 s solve is out of scope, so the docs are my only source.
entries.suggested_fix: State in the root README's seeds section whether seeds apply to private_inputs (they do), and correct section 4, section 7, section 8 and both comments in evolvekit.real.yaml. Optionally allow 'private_seeds: 1'.

entries.title: `run` output is block-buffered when redirected: the log file stays empty until the process exits
entries.step: Running the offline example in the background with output to a log file and tailing it from a second shell
entries.command: ( time ./.venv-pyvrp/Scripts/python.exe -m evolvekit run --config examples/pyvrp/evolvekit.yaml --run-dir "$S/runs/pyvrp" ) > "$S/run.log" 2>&1     then in a second shell: cat "$S/run.log"
entries.observed: cat run.log printed nothing at 16:56:12, 16:56:30, 16:56:52, 16:57:07, 16:57:15 and 16:57:35, although runs.jsonl already had 3 rows (generation 1 complete) at 16:57:15. At exit (16:57:56) the whole log appeared at once, starting 'gen 0  seed        score=-2100.53 / gen 1  2 child(ren)  best=-2100.53  cells=2  spent=$0.0027'.
entries.expected: Each 'gen N' line to reach the log when the generation finishes, as it does on a TTY.
entries.why_it_matters: The real config is a 10-hour overnight job that everyone will run with '> run.log' or nohup. At ~150 bytes per generation an 8 KB buffer never flushes, so the log is empty all night, and if the process is killed the log is lost entirely.
entries.suggested_fix: flush=True on progress prints (or sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True) at CLI start); mention `python -u` in the README; better, also append progress lines to <run_dir>/run.log.

entries.title: `status` cannot tell me whether a run is alive, what it is evaluating, or why it stopped; finished candidates stay invisible until the generation ends
entries.step: Watching the offline run from a second shell with the documented tools
entries.command: ./.venv-pyvrp/Scripts/python.exe -m evolvekit status --run-dir "$S/runs/pyvrp"   (repeated during and after the run)
entries.observed: 16:56:12 (run alive, .lock present, seed being solved): 'no runs recorded in ...\runs\pyvrp'. 16:57:07: 'candidates   : 1 (0 rejected) ... generations  : 0 ... archive      : no archive.json snapshot yet' although work/stage_out/g001-c0002.full.json had been written at 16:56:51. Rows for both children appeared only at 16:57:15 when the generation ended. After the run: same block with 'generations  : 2', no 'finished', no stop reason, no start/end time. grep -rl "exhausted|stop_reason|stop reason" over the run dir finds nothing: 'stop reason : generations exhausted' (and 'ABORT: seed failed evaluation') exist only on the run's stdout.
entries.expected: A state line (running pid N since HH:MM / finished: <stop reason> / dead lock), the candidate, stage, seed currently being evaluated with elapsed time, and rows appended as each candidate finishes.
entries.why_it_matters: With evolvekit.real.yaml one generation is 2+ hours, so `status` is frozen for hours and I cannot distinguish a hung PyVRP solve from a healthy one, nor learn next morning why the run ended if the terminal is gone (especially combined with the buffered log).
entries.suggested_fix: Have status read .lock and report liveness; write a small <run_dir>/state.json (current candidate/stage/seed, started_at, last heartbeat, stop_reason at exit); append each candidate's row when its cascade ends rather than at generation end (or write a provisional row).

entries.title: No documented way to see which PyVRP parameters a candidate actually used or how they differ from the defaults
entries.step: Answering 'what did the best candidate change relative to PyVRP defaults?'
entries.command: python -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir "$S/runs/pyvrp"; python -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir "$S/runs/own" --html "$S/own-board.html"; then by hand: cd $S/runs/pyvrp/work/candidates && diff g000-c0001.py g001-c0003.py
entries.observed: Leaderboard columns are '| # | id | gen | rank | score | cell | operator | model | lineage | gap | USD |' - no objective, no parameters. The HTML has the same columns; it embeds the rows in <script id="rows" type="application/json"> but nothing renders kpis or the block. The stage_out JSON has only 'kpis' and 'text_feedback'; neither contains the resolved SolveParams. The manual diff is ~130 lines, mostly the deleted docstring, with the real changes buried ('num_iters_no_improvement=60_000', 'num_neighbours=35', 'symmetric_proximity=False', ...). work/candidates/ is not mentioned in the README's run-directory description.
entries.expected: A per-candidate table 'parameter | PyVRP default | effective value on instance X', emitted by the evaluator (it has the SolveParams object in hand) and shown by leaderboard/HTML, plus the operator list diff.
entries.why_it_matters: The deliverable of tuning PyVRP is a parameter set. Candidates are code and may compute values from data.num_clients / time_limit (the section 8 winner did), so reading the source does not give the numbers used on a given instance; I would have to write my own introspection script.
entries.suggested_fix: In skeleton.run_solve, serialise the returned SolveParams (ils/penalty/neighbourhood/perturbation fields + operator names) into the stage JSON and a 'params vs default' line in text_feedback; add `evolvekit show <id> --run-dir` that prints KPIs, feedback and a block diff against the seed with docstrings ignored; document work/candidates and work/stage_out.

entries.title: Extending the example to a test set of N instances is undocumented and the evaluator's aggregation hides per-instance results
entries.step: Building a test set (3 instances here, 10 intended) with several seeds and a fixed time limit per instance
entries.command: cp examples/pyvrp/{evaluate.py,skeleton.py,make_instance.py,fake_responses.yaml,evolvekit.yaml} $S/own/; make_instance.py --orders 80 --seed {1,2,3}; edited INPUT_SETS in my copy of evaluate.py to add "test3"; own.yaml with 'inputs: [test3]', 'seeds: 2', '--seed {seed} --time-limit 3'; python -m evolvekit preflight --config own.yaml
entries.observed: It works, but only after reading evaluate.py: set names map to file names in a hard-coded INPUT_SETS dict resolved against evaluate.py's own directory (an instance generated elsewhere, like my $S/instance-3000-s7.json, cannot be named on the command line). Per seed file: 'objective 913.505... convergence [971.1798, 971.1798, 971.1798, 971.1798]' - objective is the raw mean over instances, convergence is the first instance only, there is no per-instance list KPI; per-instance numbers exist only as prose, 'len(text_feedback) 1050' for 3 instances (~350 chars each) and the framework truncates at 2,000 chars, so from about the 6th instance on they are cut; preflight already showed '| ... 4 more line(s)'. Instances run sequentially inside one process, so the per-run timeout must cover N x time-limit ('19.1s x2 seed(s)' for 3 x 3 s x 2).
entries.expected: A README section 'use your own instance set': how to add instances (ideally --inputs accepting paths/globs), that --time-limit is per instance and timeout is per seed-run so timeout >= 1.5 x N x T, how objectives are aggregated (raw mean lets large instances dominate; no gap-to-baseline normalisation), and a per-instance list KPI such as objective_per_instance as the root README recommends ('bins_per_instance').
entries.why_it_matters: A single-instance tuning result is not something I can defend; a test set is the first thing an OR engineer needs. What the docs do give me ({inputs}, seeds: N, {seed}, kpi_cv, timeout per run) is generic; everything PyVRP-specific I had to infer from evaluate.py, and the instance JSON schema for bringing real data is documented nowhere but make_instance.py.
entries.suggested_fix: Add the README section; accept instance file paths in --inputs; emit objective_per_instance / iterations_per_instance list KPIs and a normalised mean (ratio to a stored defaults baseline); shorten per-instance feedback so 10+ instances fit in 2,000 chars.

entries.title: No documented support for parallel evaluation or CPU-core management
entries.step: Looking for a way to evaluate candidates / seeds / instances in parallel without oversubscribing cores
entries.command: grep -i -E "parallel|worker|concurren|thread|n_jobs|cores?|affinity|oversubscri" README.md AGENTS.md docs/*.md examples/**/*.md examples/**/*.yaml ; python -m evolvekit run --help
entries.observed: Only hits: 'single-threaded' (pyvrp README section 5) and 'one core saturated for fifteen minutes' (section 7). run --help offers only --config, --run-dir, --generations, --quiet. Observed behaviour is fully sequential: seed files written 10 s apart ('g000-c0001.full.seed0.json 17:03:10', '...seed1.json 17:03:20'), children one after another, instances in a for-loop inside evaluate.py.
entries.expected: A documented knob (e.g. evaluate.max_parallel / per-stage workers) that caps concurrent solver processes at physical cores minus one, ideally with affinity pinning, plus a warning that on a wall-clock-bounded solver oversubscription silently lowers scores (the README's own section 5 caveat).
entries.why_it_matters: 10 instances x 3 seeds x 60 s is 30 min per candidate on one core of a many-core workstation. If I parallelise inside my own evaluate.py I have no guidance on keeping scores comparable, and two evolvekit runs side by side would contaminate each other's scores without any warning.
entries.suggested_fix: Add a bounded process pool across seeds and across same-generation candidates for command stages, default 1, documented with the oversubscription caveat; record the concurrency level and iterations/second in each row so contaminated evaluations can be spotted.

entries.title: Per-seed and per-instance results are only recoverable from undocumented files
entries.step: Checking whether per-seed / per-instance results of a seeds: 2 stage are visible
entries.command: ls $S/runs/own/work/stage_out/ ; python -m evolvekit status --run-dir $S/runs/own ; python -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir $S/runs/own
entries.observed: Files 'g000-c0001.full.seed0.json', 'g000-c0001.full.seed1.json', ... exist under work/stage_out (seed0 objective 913.5, seed1 880.0). runs.jsonl keeps only the mean, kpi_cv and the first seed's feedback. status/leaderboard/HTML show none of it (visible HTML text is just id/gen/rank/score/cell/operator/model/lineage/inspirations/gap/tok/USD and the grid). The README's run-directory description lists runs.jsonl, usage.jsonl, archive.json, scratchpad.md, .lock and traces/ but not work/.
entries.expected: Documented location of per-seed outputs, and a view (leaderboard --kpis objective,iterations or an HTML detail row) showing per-seed values, CV and per-instance numbers.
entries.why_it_matters: I found the files only because I was listing the directory while the run was live. kpi_cv is described as being there 'so a human can see when the mean was a coin toss' but no tool shows it to a human.
entries.suggested_fix: Document work/candidates and work/stage_out in the README; add --kpis to leaderboard and render kpis/kpi_cv/feedback from the already-embedded rows JSON in the HTML.

entries.title: preflight and run print only 'exit code 1' for a failed stage; the evaluator's stderr is hidden
entries.observed:
'stage full                 FAILED  0.3s  (timeout 60s per run)
    failure : exit code 1
...
FAILURE : stage full: exit code 1
verdict : failures (1 failure(s), 0 warning(s))'. `run` likewise: 'ABORT: seed failed evaluation ... stage full: exit code 1'. The real message ('this evaluator needs pyvrp >= 0.14; ...python.exe does not have it and there is no .venv-pyvrp above ...own. Create one: ...') was only found by re-running the stage command by hand; for `run` it is in runs.jsonl under last_failure, for preflight it is nowhere (temporary directory).
entries.expected: The last ~10 lines of the stage's stderr printed under 'failure :'.
entries.why_it_matters: evaluate.py's message was excellent and would have solved the problem in seconds; instead I had to reconstruct the command with {candidate}/{out}/{seed} substituted manually.
entries.suggested_fix: Print the stderr tail (already captured) in preflight and in the run's ABORT line; mention last_failure in the README.

entries.title: `run` exits 0 after 'ABORT: seed failed evaluation'
entries.step: Running my own config while its evaluator was broken
entries.observed: 'exit=0' with log 'gen 0  seed        score=-1e+09 / ABORT: seed failed evaluation (mojibake dash) fix the harness before spending: stage full: exit code 1', followed by a normal-looking leaderboard and summary with 'best score  : -1e+09'.
entries.expected: Non-zero exit (preflight documents 0/1/2; run documents only 3 for the lock).
entries.why_it_matters: I batch experiments from scripts; `run && export-winner` would carry on with a run that never evaluated anything.
entries.suggested_fix: Exit 2 on seed failure / provider halt, and document run's exit codes next to preflight's.

entries.title: Copying the example out of the repo (as docs/new-experiment.md recommends) breaks the stage command's interpreter lookup
entries.step: Starting my own experiment from a copy of examples/pyvrp in another directory
entries.observed: 'this evaluator needs pyvrp >= 0.14; C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe does not have it and there is no .venv-pyvrp above ...\pyvrp-example\own.' (bare `python` is the system interpreter, which here carries PyVRP 0.13.4). I fixed it by hard-coding 'C:/Users/<user>/studio/evolvekit/.venv-pyvrp/Scripts/python.exe evaluate.py ...' in the stage command, which the README says a config should not do.
entries.expected: A portable way to say 'the interpreter running evolvekit', e.g. a {python} placeholder, since the README already requires evolvekit itself to run from .venv-pyvrp.
entries.why_it_matters: Cost about five minutes, mostly because the message was hidden (previous entry). Anyone whose experiments live outside the evolvekit checkout hits it.
entries.suggested_fix: Add a {python} placeholder resolving to sys.executable and use it in all example configs; keep evaluate.py's relaunch as a fallback; mention an env override such as EVOLVEKIT_PYVRP_PYTHON.

entries.title: `extends` merges search.operators, so an intended param_lhs-only (zero-LLM) child config still makes LLM calls
entries.step: Making a zero-LLM variant of the example
entries.command: own.yaml: 'extends: evolvekit.yaml' + 'search: {operators: {param_lhs: 1.0}}'; python -m evolvekit run --config own.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/own
entries.observed: Leaderboard: 'g001-c0002 | ... | rewrite | fake-small' and 'g002-c0004 | ... | rewrite | fake-small'; summary 'spend       : $0.0025 over 2 call(s), 14761 token(s)'. The inherited diff 0.4 / rewrite 0.3 / crossover 0.2 stayed active.
entries.expected: Either a documented zero-LLM recipe or a warning when a child config's operator map is merged with inherited non-zero shares.
entries.why_it_matters: With a paid provider in the base file this silently spends money. The README does document key-by-key merging, but param_lhs is advertised as 'the operator that costs no tokens at all' with no recipe for running it alone, and the task's machine has no API keys.
entries.suggested_fix: Document 'operators: {diff: 0, rewrite: 0, crossover: 0, param_lhs: 1}' as the zero-LLM recipe (or add a --no-llm flag); print the effective operator shares at run start.

entries.title: No export of the winner; README references a winner file no documented command produces
entries.step: Getting the best configuration out of a finished run
entries.observed: Subcommands are '{init,preflight,run,status,leaderboard}' - no export/best/show. README section 8 cites 'runs/pyvrp-real-1/winner-g004-c0015.py in the run directory', but my run dirs contain no winner-*.py, only work/candidates/<id>.py. preflight --help says candidates are 'saved under a run's candidates/ directory'; the real path is work/candidates/.
entries.expected: `evolvekit export --run-dir R [--id X] --out best.py` (or the run writing best.py at exit), and a correct path in the help text.
entries.why_it_matters: The thing I take away from a tuning run is the winning configure() block; I should not need to guess that work/candidates/<leaderboard id>.py is it.
entries.suggested_fix: Add the export command, write <run_dir>/best.py at exit, fix the --candidate help text, and say in section 8 how the winner file was made.

entries.title: preflight KPI line hides the objective and reports an unnamed 'noisiest KPI'; seed timing is ambiguous
entries.step: Reading preflight output for the offline config and my multi-seed config
entries.command: python -m evolvekit preflight --config examples/pyvrp/evolvekit.yaml ; python -m evolvekit preflight --config own.yaml
entries.observed: 'kpis    : budget_s=20, clients_visited=295, config_errors=0, configure_s=0.0001601, distance=1.09722e+06, distance_cost=329.164, ... 21 more' - alphabetical, so `objective` (the score KPI) is never shown. 'note    : stage full ran 2 seed(s); the noisiest KPI varied by 44.77% across them.' does not say which KPI (objective CV was ~2.6 %). 'stage full  ok  19.1s x2 seed(s)  (timeout 60s per run)' - 19.1 s is the total for both seeds, not per run.
entries.expected: score.objective and penalty KPIs listed first with their CV; the noisiest KPI named (and signature_ignore'd timing KPIs excluded); per-run duration shown.
entries.why_it_matters: The numbers I need for a go/no-go (objective, its noise, per-run time against the per-run timeout) are the ones not shown.
entries.suggested_fix: Order KPIs: objective, penalty KPIs, descriptors, then the rest; name the noisiest KPI and also print the objective's CV; print 'N.Ns per run x2'.

entries.title: Stale statements in examples/pyvrp (text_feedback / {seed} 'not landed yet', matrix size, branch name)
entries.step: Reading the example's README, config and evaluator docstring against observed behaviour
entries.command: loaded $S/instance-3000-s7.json via skeleton.load_instance/build_data and printed data.num_locations; inspected runs.jsonl 'feedback'
entries.observed: README section 3: 'The framework reads payload["kpis"] and ignores the rest today ... once text_feedback lands' and evaluate.py docstring 'the framework is growing a {seed} placeholder', evolvekit.yaml comment 'once the framework grows the {seed} placeholder' - but runs.jsonl has 'feedback : {"full": "metro-300-s7: feasible, ...' and seeds/{seed} worked for me. README sections 5 and 7 say '3,003 x 3,003 matrices'; actual: 'num_clients 3030 num_depots 3 num_locations 3105 ... distance matrix shape (3105, 3105)'. Section 7 says the example 'lives on examples/pyvrp' (branch); I am on integration/expensive-tuning.
entries.expected: Docs matching the current framework and instance.
entries.why_it_matters: Made me doubt whether seeds: N and evaluator notes were usable on this example until I tried them.
entries.suggested_fix: Update the three 'not landed yet' passages, change 3,003 to 3,105 (and the 750 MB estimate if derived from it), drop the branch remark.

entries.title: README commands are bash-only on a Windows-only layout
entries.step: Pasting section 6 commands into PowerShell, the default Windows shell
entries.command: powershell -NoProfile -File paste-test.ps1   (contains the README's two-line '.venv-pyvrp/Scripts/python -m evolvekit run \' + '    --config examples/pyvrp/evolvekit.yaml --run-dir ...')  and  python -c "from pathlib import Path; print(Path('/tmp/kpis.json').resolve())" from PowerShell
entries.observed: 'Missing expression after unary operator '--'.' / 'Unexpected token 'config' in expression or statement.' exit=1. '/tmp/kpis.json' resolves to 'C:\tmp\kpis.json' from PowerShell (evaluate.py would mkdir it), whereas Git Bash rewrites it to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. Both worked for me only because I used Git Bash.
entries.expected: One-line commands, or PowerShell variants, and an --out path that means the same thing in both shells (e.g. runs/kpis.json).
entries.why_it_matters: The interpreter path (.venv-pyvrp/Scripts/python) says Windows, the syntax says bash; a Windows user without Git Bash fails on the first command.
entries.suggested_fix: Put each command on one line; replace /tmp/kpis.json with runs/pyvrp-baseline/kpis.json.

entries.title: Leaderboard 'cell' column goes stale after auto re-binning, making the archive grid look wrong
entries.step: Reading the HTML/markdown leaderboard of my own run
entries.observed: Table: 'g000-c0001 | 0 | -900.102 | ... | 0,2' and 'g001-c0002 | 1 | -906.652 | ... | 0,2', yet the grid and archive.json give cell [0,2] 'elite: g001-c0002, fitness -906.65, occupants 2' - apparently a worse elite than the seed in the 'same' cell. archive.json shows why: complexity range re-binned to [2541, 2626], so the seed (complexity 2626) now sits in row 3; the row's stored cell is from insertion time.
entries.expected: The cell column to reflect the current binning (or be labelled 'cell at insert').
entries.why_it_matters: Cost a few minutes wondering whether the archive was keeping the wrong elite.
entries.suggested_fix: Recompute cells for display from the current descriptor ranges, or show both.

entries.title: Offline demo: no stated expected outcome, param_lhs never fires, one child's -2600 score is unexplained, mojibake in ABORT line, unreadable make_instance --help
entries.step: Judging whether the two-minute offline run 'worked'

ABORT line prints 'seed failed evaluation � fix the harness' (cp1252 dash) when redirected. make_instance.py --help reflows its whole module docstring into one 35-line paragraph.

unanswered_questions: Is the run alive right now, and which candidate / stage / seed / instance is it evaluating? How long has the current evaluation been running and what is the ETA for the generation and the run?
Why did a finished run stop, and when did it start and end? The stop reason is printed once on stdout and is not persisted in the run directory or shown by status.
What effective SolveParams did candidate X hand to PyVRP on instance Y (especially when configure() computes them from data.num_clients or time_limit), and how do they differ from PyVRP's defaults?
What was each candidate's objective per instance and per seed as numbers (not prose), and on which instances does the winner beat or lose to the seed?
Is a reported improvement distinguishable from noise? kpi_cv is only in runs.jsonl; no view shows it, and there is no paired comparison against the incumbent.
Was the machine under load during a given evaluation? iterations is recorded but no view shows iterations or iterations per second relative to the seed.
What does one full-stage evaluation of evolvekit.real.yaml really cost (30, 45 or 61 minutes)? I could only infer 4 x 900 s from a scaled-down config; the docs give three different answers.
Can evaluations (candidates, seeds, instances) run in parallel, how do I cap them to physical cores or pin them, and how would parallelism affect a wall-clock-bounded score? Nothing is documented.

How do I bring my own instances (VRPLIB files or company data)? The instance JSON schema is defined only implicitly by make_instance.py, and evaluate.py only accepts hard-coded set names resolved next to itself.

Does param_lhs sample linearly or log-uniformly over ranges like MAX_PENALTY [1000, 10000000]? Can # PARAMS declare integer, log-scale, boolean (exhaustive_on_best) or categorical (operator subset) parameters?
Is there a supported zero-LLM mode (param_lhs only) that needs no models block at all?
Once an LLM rewrite drops the # PARAMS line (as the scripted demo children do), are that lineage's descendants permanently excluded from param_lhs?
How was winner-g004-c0015.py in README section 8 produced, and is there a supported way to export and re-run the best candidate standalone?
How does resume behave on this example (mid-generation kill during a 900 s solve)? Not tried in this session.
How should objectives be aggregated across instances of different sizes (the example takes a raw mean), and can the score be a gap to a stored defaults baseline per instance?
went_well: The section-6 offline command worked first time: 1m50s against a documented 'about two minutes', exit 0, no network, nothing written into the repo.
Baseline reproduction matched the README exactly: 'objective EUR 2,076' (2075.5296 vs README 2,075.5), 9 routes / 13 trips, convergence 2,180 -> 2,150 -> 2,076 -> 2,076.

evaluate.py's self-relaunch into .venv-pyvrp worked transparently inside the repo even though bare `python` here is a system interpreter with PyVRP 0.13.4, and its own error message when no venv is found is precise and actionable.

preflight is genuinely useful: per-stage KPIs, the evaluator's notes, durations, per-KPI CV on seeds stages, a clean/warn/fail verdict with documented exit codes, and an unprompted note that a wall-clock-bounded evaluator turns CPU contention into solution quality.

`run` refuses to continue when the seed fails ('ABORT: seed failed evaluation ... fix the harness before spending') instead of breeding children into a broken evaluator; stderr is captured in runs.jsonl last_failure.
make_instance.py is fast (0.34 s for 3,000 orders), prints a useful one-line summary (3030 clients, 36 shipments, 261 vehicles of 12 types from 3 depots), and the instance loaded into PyVRP in 1.3 s.
seeds: N with {seed} worked on the first try on my own config; per-seed output files are written and kpi_cv is recorded per KPI; the hold-out stage is preflighted too.
evaluate.py already loops over multi-instance input sets, so a test set needed only one added INPUT_SETS line in my copy.
text_feedback is high quality for an OR reader: feasibility, iterations, convergence quarters, fleet mix, dropped optional orders, overtime.
`extends` worked from a sibling file in my scratch directory, and status/leaderboard could be run against a live run directory without disturbing it; the lock was released cleanly on exit.
param_lhs produced free children with the sampled constants plainly visible at the top of the block, which makes those candidates easy to read.
Time from opening the docs to my own (non-shipped) multi-instance, multi-seed problem completing a run was about 9 minutes.
